_about: Numbers from the 31-VM GCP run of 2026-10-30 (benchmarks/scale_test.py and benchmarks/lightning_comparison/scaling_run.py). Raw logs are in this directory.
fleet: 1 server (n1-standard-4, gpulayer up --no-worker) and 30 workers (n1-standard-4, 4 slots each): 23 in europe-west1-b, 7 in europe-west4-a; Python 3.12, torch 2.15.0 CPU, Lightning 2.6.6

strong_scaling.subtitle: A CNN on 32,768 images, 2 epochs; GCP n1-standard-4, 4 processes per machine, gloo; same machines for both
strong_scaling.method: Wall time from start until the last process exits, median of 3 interleaved runs, both trainers on the same machines (GPUlayer pinned with worker_ids). benchmarks/results/2026-10-30-gcp-9vm/strong-scaling-pinned.log. An earlier unpinned run (strong-scaling.log here, and strong-scaling-unpinned.log in the 9vm folder) differed by up to 9% in either direction because the trainers ran on different VMs.

submit.subtitle: 30 workers, 120 slots, client with 16 threads on the server VM
submit.note: before: scale-test-before-fixes.log; after: scale-test-served-mode.log (sweep) and scale-test-sync-normal.log (shards, tiny jobs). The tiny-job burst is limited by the server process using one CPU core at 100-113% (measured with top), about 25 jobs/s.

burst_after_server_fixes.fleet: 1 server + 8 workers (n1-standard-4, 32 slots), europe-west1-b, all Intel Haswell
